positions.thesis: Down 28% year and 34% below highs means significant bad news is already priced in. Enterprise software leader has strong long-term fundamentals and likely to recover.
evidence: about 34% below its high of the past year, so some bad news is already reflected in the price
positions.counterargument: Continued weakness could indicate structural damage rather than temporary pullback; recovery not guaranteed.

positions.thesis: Strong 37% annual gain demonstrates market confidence. Recent 11% monthly pullback is normal profit-taking after a big rally. iPhone ecosystem and services are durable.
positions.counterargument: Already rallied significantly, could see further profit-taking and consolidation.

positions.thesis: E-commerce and cloud leadership with 7% year gain shows consistent performance. Down 14% month but the business model is sound and diversified.
positions.counterargument: Recent 14% monthly decline suggests weakness in consumer spending or cloud spending.

positions.thesis: Healthcare leader up 65% year with continued 6% monthly gain shows momentum. Healthcare is defensive and diversified across pharma, devices, and consumer.
positions.counterargument: Already significantly appreciated, could be vulnerable to profit-taking.

positions.thesis: AI and semiconductor leader up 27% year. Only down 9% month shows relative strength. Critical infrastructure role in data centers supports long-term thesis.
positions.counterargument: AI sector valuations may be stretched; semiconductor cycle could turn negative.

positions.thesis: Eli Lilly up 43% year with continued 6% monthly strength. Pharmaceutical leadership and diversified pipeline provides defensive healthcare exposure.
positions.counterargument: Trading near 52-week highs limits downside protection and offers limited margin of safety.

positions.thesis: JPMorgan up 20% year with strong 9% monthly gain shows financial sector strength. Largest U.S. bank with diversified revenue and solid capital position.
evidence: trading close to its highest point of the past year
positions.counterargument: Already near highs with limited upside and increasing interest rate volatility risk.

positions.thesis: Berkshire Hathaway's flat performance provides stability and safety in an uncertain market. Warren Buffett's capital allocation and investor protection offer downside cushion.
positions.counterargument: No positive momentum; capital sitting in cash may lag market if recovery accelerates.

positions.thesis: Broadcom up 44% year with 21% decline from highs suggests meaningful bad news priced in. Semiconductor leader in demand for 5G and data center infrastructure.
evidence: about 21% below its high of the past year, so some bad news is already reflected in the price
positions.counterargument: Semiconductor cycle may have further downside; valuations could compress further.

positions.thesis: Coca-Cola up 19% year with only 1% monthly change shows stability. Consumer staple with global reach and pricing power for defensive positioning.
positions.counterargument: Limited growth; mature company with modest upside potential.

positions.thesis: PepsiCo up 13% year with only 3% monthly decline demonstrates resilience. Diversified beverages and snacks with global consumer reach.
positions.counterargument: Defensive positioning offers limited upside in bull market.

positions.thesis: Verizon up 17% year with modest 5% monthly decline is stable. Dividend telecom with reliable cash flows and defensive characteristics.
positions.counterargument: Limited growth; mature regulated utility with low upside.

reasoning: As a nervous investor concerned about losses, I concentrated on quality large-cap companies with demonstrated market confidence and defensive characteristics. I weighted value opportunities (MSFT at 34% discount, AVGO at 21% discount) alongside stable performers (AAPL, AMZN, healthcare leaders JNJ/LLY) and holding significant 42% cash as a buffer against further uncertainty. I avoided severely beaten-down stocks (ADBE, ADSK, ORCL) and momentum extremes, trusting that the market's judgment on major established companies offers better odds than speculative plays.
